# Data classification

*Generated by `p5_governance/bootstrap/render_classification.py` from `p5_governance/classification.yml`, the silver contract and
`p5_governance/gold_columns.json`. Do not edit by hand: a test fails when this file is stale. Classes are as the design says (6.7).*

| Class | Meaning | May leave the project? |
|---|---|---|
| **public** | OFF's own public content, or an aggregate of it | Yes, but only through the exit function (`silver_lib/egress.py`), with the OFF attribution and ODbL notice |
| **personal** | identifies a person, or could once a reader joins it with OFF's public data; pseudonymised data is still personal data | No |
| **internal** | operating data: lineage and run bookkeeping | Not published |

## What this does and does not say
- It is a **label on every column**, not a guarantee. OFF itself publishes contributor usernames, so the hashed codes protect only against
  our own readers, and the scrub of free text is a **measured bound, not a guarantee** (`product_name` and `brands` are public; the measured
  residue of contact-shaped text and long digit runs is in the privacy audit, step 6).
- `personal` columns are also protected by code: `egress: never` in the silver contract, a column mask in Unity Catalog (`policies.yml`),
  and a test that no gold column is personal. The classes `public` and `internal` are policy; the exit function drops only `egress: never` columns today.
- Pseudonymised data stays personal data. Nothing here claims anonymisation or compliance with any law.

## Silver: `workspace.packsense_silver.silver_product_versions`

81 columns: 64 public, 10 personal, 7 internal. The class comes from the `class` column of `p2_lakehouse/contracts/silver.yml` (key and public to public, hashed to **personal**, lineage to internal, derived to public), except that a column that never leaves silver and is not a hashed identity is internal.

| Column | Class | Never leaves silver | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | public |  | barcode as text, never a number (leading zeros) |
| `code_kind` | public |  | gtin8 \| gtin12 \| gtin13 \| gtin14 \| other, from the length of code; other = lengths 15-39, ~0.2% of rows, kept (real products such as weighed items) |
| `last_modified_t` | public |  | unix seconds |
| `created_t` | public |  |  |
| `schema_version` | public |  | 1004 on every sampled row; any other value is reported by the drift monitor |
| `rev` | public |  |  |
| `product_type` | public |  | 'food' on every sampled row |
| `lc` | public |  | main language code; $.lang is identical and not kept |
| `product_name` | public |  | absent on 6% of rows; 197 empty strings; p99 length 66 |
| `brands` | public |  | absent on 18% of rows; own-handle redaction does NOT apply here (producer accounts write their own brand) |
| `quantity_amount` | public |  | amount per pack; NULL when the value does not parse (10.9% of the 41,329 non-empty values on all of bronze) |
| `quantity_unit` | public |  | canonical unit from the parsing.units map |
| `quantity_multiplier` | public |  | packs in a multipack, e.g. 6 for '6 x 33 cl'; NULL for a single pack |
| `serving_amount` | public |  | first amount in g or ml found in serving_size; NULL when there is none |
| `serving_unit` | public |  | 'g' or 'ml' |
| `ingredients_sha256` | public |  | SHA-256 of the normalised ingredients text; NULL when there is none (56% of rows). Detects a change in ingredients; the text itself stays in bronze |
| `product_quantity` | public |  | int, float or (9 of 25,000) string in the raw data |
| `serving_quantity` | public |  | int, float, null or string in the raw data |
| `product_quantity_unit` | public |  | v4: unit of product_quantity as OFF normalises it; 3 distinct values (g, ml and one more); present on 41% of versions |
| `categories_tags` | public |  | absent on 51% of rows |
| `countries_tags` | public |  | absent on 0.25% of rows |
| `labels_tags` | public |  |  |
| `allergens_tags` | public |  | feeds the allergen change log; empty list on 73% of rows is a real value (no allergens declared) |
| `traces_tags` | public |  |  |
| `states_tags` | public |  | OFF's completeness state tags |
| `data_quality_errors_tags` | public |  | OFF's own error-level flags; the split by severity is kept (the union data_quality_tags is not: gold can rebuild it) |
| `data_quality_warnings_tags` | public |  |  |
| `data_quality_info_tags` | public |  |  |
| `data_quality_bugs_tags` | public |  |  |
| `additives_tags` | public |  | v4: OFF's additive ids (en:e412); non-empty on 21% of versions |
| `ingredients_analysis_tags` | public |  | v4: vegan / vegetarian / palm-oil verdicts; present on 40% of versions |
| `nutrient_levels_tags` | public |  | v4: OFF's low / moderate / high verdict per nutrient (fat, saturated fat, sugars, salt); OFF's own judgement, for comparing with our rules |
| `food_groups_tags` | public |  | v4: OFF's food-group hierarchy, newer than pnns_groups |
| `packaging_tags` | public |  | v4: user-typed pack description tags; present on 14% of versions, 99.2% pass the shape |
| `origins_tags` | public |  | v4: user-typed origin tags; non-empty on 7% of versions; 13.5% of values (free text with spaces) fail the shape and are dropped. Provisional: residue measured on the v4 rebuild before it is switched on |
| `pnns_groups_1` | public |  | 'unknown' is a real value on 60% of rows |
| `pnns_groups_2` | public |  |  |
| `nutriscore_grade` | public |  | a-e, 'unknown' (61%), 'not-applicable' |
| `nutriscore_score` | public |  | present on 36% of rows |
| `nova_group` | public |  | 1-4, present on 35% of rows |

## Other tables

### `workspace.packsense_bronze.bronze_delta_raw`: internal

the landed OFF record exactly as received, so it still holds the plaintext contributor names. 6 columns: 2 public, 1 personal, 3 internal.

| Column | Class | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | public |  |
| `last_modified_t` | public |  |
| `raw_json` | personal | the whole OFF record; carries plaintext contributor usernames (OFF publishes them, but this copy is never read by analysts, gold or any export) |

### `workspace.packsense_bronze.bronze_manifest`: internal

file-level load bookkeeping. 7 columns: 0 public, 0 personal, 7 internal.

### `workspace.packsense_silver.silver_quarantine`: internal

records that could not be loaded, with a coded reason. 11 columns: 2 public, 1 personal, 8 internal.

| Column | Class | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | public |  |
| `last_modified_t` | public |  |
| `payload` | personal | the record content kept for diagnosis, scrubbed of patterns but not of everything: analysts and gold are denied this table (grants and nightly policy checks) |

### `workspace.packsense_silver.silver_manifest`: internal

per-file processing bookkeeping. 7 columns: 0 public, 0 personal, 7 internal.

### `workspace.packsense_snapshots.snapshot_flag_events`: public

which OFF quality flags appeared or disappeared on which product between two weekly snapshots of OFF's public dataset (barcode, flag tag, edit time; no contributor field). 12 columns: 12 public, 0 personal, 0 internal.

### `workspace.packsense_snapshots.snapshot_open_counts`: public

how many products carried each flag tag at one snapshot (an aggregate of OFF's public flags). 6 columns: 6 public, 0 personal, 0 internal.

### `workspace.packsense_snapshots.snapshot_presence_events`: public

barcodes that were in one weekly snapshot of OFF and not in the next (deletion candidates). 6 columns: 6 public, 0 personal, 0 internal.

### `workspace.packsense_snapshots.snapshot_manifest`: internal

per-pair bookkeeping of the snapshot comparison (counts, bytes read, run id). 16 columns: 0 public, 0 personal, 16 internal.

whether each product we hold is still in OFF's food database (a barcode and a status; from a snapshot of OFF's public dataset and from OFF's public API). 7 columns: 4 public, 0 personal, 3 internal.

| Column | Class | Note |
